name: Do LLMs Feel? Emotion Circuits (Wang et al.)
ontology_notes: Not a memory store. Emotion is six Ekman labels (anger, sadness, happiness, fear, surprise, disgust) implemented as residual-stream directions plus sparse neuron and attention-head circuits. SEV is a scenario-event dataset, not a user or relationship ontology.

ontology.evidence: SEV has eight domains, 20 scenarios, three valences (paper §4). Types are emotions, not memory kinds. scripts/02_emotion_direction_extraction/2_compute_emotion_directions.py writes v_e,attn and v_e,mlp. No user/character/relationship tables.
ontology.label: measured

write_policy.evidence: Directions are mean residual after subtracting the six-emotion group mean (paper §5). Circuits are assembled with a budget of ten times the sublayer count (paper §7.2, scripts/06_emotion_circuit_integration/5_integrate_global_circuit.py). Modulation writes delta vectors into selected neurons and heads at the last token (paper §7.3, 1_enhance_global_circuit.py).
write_policy.label: measured

read_policy.evidence: Generation-time circuit modulation with lambda=1.0 and greedy decoding, no emotion instruction in the prompt (paper §7.3). Residual steering baseline injects v_e at layers 11-20 with alpha=8 (paper §5). quick_start.py --emotion selects a target at inference.
read_policy.label: measured

supersession.evidence: A new target emotion replaces the previous modulation. No stored fact is invalidated.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: No timestamps or validity windows. SEV events are static vignettes.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: One instruct model. Emotions are not user vs character vs relationship identities.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Ablation zeros the top-k emotion neurons or heads and drops the projection score s (paper §6.3, Fig. 3). That can suppress expression. It is not a retrieve-time skip of a high-score memory for trauma or spoilers. The shipped control mostly induces emotion (99.65% expression accuracy), not socially timed quiet.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: No filter, provenance, or trust tags. Circuit control can force an emotion onto arbitrary inputs, which is a hijack surface, not a defense.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: No forget-that. Ablation is a temporary hook, not deletion of stored state.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Discovery dumps residuals, ranks neurons and heads, then scores sublayer importance. Online cost is hooks on a sparse circuit during greedy decode. Judge is GPT-4o-mini. Paper does not publish per-turn token budgets for a companion prompt.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: GPL-3.0 LICENSE. Main model is LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct. Appendix H repeats on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Intimate chat can stay on one machine. Copyleft applies if you distribute. Labeling used GPT-4o-mini.
local.label: measured

mcp.evidence: Research repo. No MCP server in the tree.
mcp.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Stealable control for hole 2. Emotion is a circuit you can induce or ablate, not a retrieved mood adjective. That is a possible silence layer for expression. It is not a companion memory system. Eval is Ekman label accuracy on SEV-style text, not socially wrong recall of a fact.

published_eval.name: Held-out SEV-style test set, GPT-4o-mini judged emotion-expression accuracy (six Ekman emotions)
published_eval.claimed_score: Circuit modulation 99.65% overall (paper §7.3, Appendix D Table 2). Residual steering 91.22% (paper §5). Prompting about 99% on SEV and the test set. Surprise steering only 67.71%, circuit 100%.
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Whether generated text is labeled as the target emotion under matched scenario-event prompts. Not companion silence, identity drift, or poisoning.

open_unknowns: Whether ablating a circuit mid-conversation can refuse to emote without collapsing helpfulness, which the paper does not test as a companion silence policy.
Circuit stability after character-card finetune, listed as a limitation in the paper.
